newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil steady, still lagging behind crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil steady, still lagging behind crude.

text.p: Fuel oil was steady but quiet on Wednesday. Support from strong crude balanced slack physical demand on cargoes, but fuel failed to match crude's gains.
Good bunker demand helped propel high sulphur barges to $129 fob ARA early, but the market looked shaky. When sellers started to outnumber buyers the prices eased off $1 or so.
High sulphur cargoes also looked narrowly weaker with little physical interest. "There's a trader out there, but I can't see anyone else who is desparate for material," said one trader.
Romanian demand for 1.2 million tonnes this winter continued to be cited as bullish support.
But nothing was seen done since last week. Improved hydro-electric power capacity may also make it less likely for Portuguse utliity EdP to tender for November barrels.
Low sulphur cracked cargoes were a touch softer in line with easier swaps at $127-128 fob NWE.

Although the spread against high sulphur narrows and against crude widens dealers maintained that prices will rise with colder weather. Congestion at Milazzo may hinder buying and one 50kt cargo that was shown earlier in the week was taken into the sellers' system.
